# Arrow IPC STREAM test fixtures

These are test data only; they do not imply support for every field type in the source schemas.

## Independent Apache Arrow C++ integration fixtures

`generated_primitive_cpp21.stream` and `generated_binary_cpp21.stream` are byte-for-byte copies of the Apache Arrow Testing repository's IPC STREAM interoperability fixtures, generated by Arrow C++ 21.0.0. Arrow's integration-test documentation describes these as cross-implementation fixtures: <https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/Integration.html>. Upstream paths:

- <https://github.com/apache/arrow-testing/blob/master/data/arrow-ipc-stream/integration/cpp-21.0.0/generated_primitive.stream>
- <https://github.com/apache/arrow-testing/blob/master/data/arrow-ipc-stream/integration/cpp-21.0.0/generated_binary.stream>

The project keeps the original fixture bytes, not regenerated copies. SHA-256 and length:

| File | Bytes | SHA-256 | Relevant source schema |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `generated_primitive_cpp21.stream` | 7,152 | `124a70f6607c24dbdb50080ba953bb0f3156e3f8f4d0ea48f58b36f86c6b6e5d` | 22 primitive fields, including nullable/non-nullable int64, float64, bool and narrower signed/unsigned integer types; 2 batches of 17 and 20 rows. |
| `generated_binary_cpp21.stream` | 13,392 | `d284f820575fdc28adaba6808a2499446ed50672122f6a47742065b0541f24d4` | binary, UTF-8 and fixed-size-binary fields, nullable and non-nullable; 2 batches of 17 and 20 rows. |

These broad source schemas intentionally exercise the rule that unsupported but scalar, unprojected columns may be ignored, while a selected field must match its declared Milena type. Nested, dictionary, extension and selected unsupported types remain rejected.

## Exact signed-int64 regression fixture

`int64_above_2_53_pyarrow23.stream` is a two-record-batch stream generated with Apache Arrow C++ 23.0.1 through the PyArrow 23.0.1 IPC writer. It has one nullable signed-int64 field `wide`, and values `9007199254740991`, `9007199254740992`, `9007199254740993`, `9223372036854775807`, and NULL across batches of 2 and 3 rows. SHA-256: `595811b8fc65f05b2972befa9a9dbde7a96ce08102b994993e80d469d50115f5` (480 bytes). The test threshold is exactly representable as a binary64 literal (`9007199254740992`); the expected projected output is exactly `9007199254740993` and `9223372036854775807`, not rounded floating-point values.

Reproduction used `pyarrow==23.0.1` (`pyarrow.cpp_version == 23.0.1`), `pyarrow.schema([pyarrow.field('wide', pyarrow.int64(), nullable=True)])`, and `pyarrow.ipc.new_stream`, writing `[9007199254740991, 9007199254740992]` then `[9007199254740993, 9223372036854775807, None]` as separate record batches. The generated binary is checked in so product tests do not depend on Python or PyArrow.

The source Apache Arrow Testing fixtures are distributed from the Apache Arrow project; see the Apache Arrow repository's license terms. The PyArrow-produced file is also test data, not a runtime dependency. Milena itself remains a native C application and never invokes Python or R.
